hero.title: Ozakboy.Gmail
hero.tagline: Gmail REST and Google OAuth in one thin async client. You keep the tokens; it keeps the HTTP.
hero.subtitle: Read Gmail, apply labels, move mail to trash and send it, from a .NET server. For the case where you want to encrypt the tokens and store them in your own database, without pulling the whole Google.Apis authentication stack in to do it.

noGoogleApis.title: No Google.Apis dependency
noGoogleApis.desc: The client asks you for one thing — a callback that hands it an access token. Where tokens live, how they are encrypted and how tenants are kept apart stays your decision; the package neither stores nor touches them.

oneScope.title: Sending needs one scope
oneScope.desc: Mail goes out through the REST messages.send endpoint: the built-in RFC 822 writer composes the message (no MimeKit), the client uploads it as multipart. So gmail.modify on its own is enough — no need to ask for full mail.google.com access just to reach SMTP or IMAP.

errors.title: No parsing error JSON yourself
errors.desc: Every non-2xx response becomes a GmailApiException carrying Google's error.reason plus IsHistoryExpired, IsUnauthorized, IsRateLimited and IsNotFound. 429 and 5xx are retried with exponential backoff before you ever see them.

asyncOnly.title: Async only
asyncOnly.desc: Every network member returns a Task, ends in Async and takes a CancellationToken. ConfigureAwait(false) all the way down, and cancellation propagates unwrapped.

targets.title: Five target frameworks
targets.desc: netstandard2.0 / 2.1 plus net8.0 / 9.0 / 10.0; netstandard2.0 covers .NET Framework 4.6.1+ as well. The only dependencies are the two Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration packages used for binding and System.Text.Json on netstandard — no MIME library since 2.0.0.

narrow.title: Deliberately narrow
narrow.desc: No token storage, no Pub/Sub push notifications, no permanent delete, no IMAP or SMTP, no Google API beyond Gmail — and no opinion about which message is an ad or a scam.
